Guntaka Satyanarayana Reddy, vs Land Acquisition Officer And
Revenue ... on 12 March, 2024

Aphc010274492023
 In The High Court Of Andhra Pradesh
 At Amaravati [3311]
 (Special Original Jurisdiction)
 Tuesday ,The Twelfth Day Of March
 Two Thousand And Twenty Four
 Present
 The Honourable Ms Justice B S Bhanumathi
 Civil Revision Petition No: 1526/2023
Between:
Guntaka Satyanarayana Reddy, ...Petitioner
 And
Land Acquisition Officer And Revenue Divisional Officer ...Respondent

entities.text:
High Court Of Andhra Pradesh
 At Amaravati
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for the Petitioner:
1. DR D VENKATA RAMANA REDDY Counsel for the Respondent:
1.
The Court made the following:
This petition is filed under Article 227 of Constitution of India against the order dated 07.03.2023 dismissing the petition in I.A.No.1369 of 2022 in LAOP.No.45 of 2015 on the file of Court of Senior Civil Judge, Vijayawada, filed under Section 151 CPC and Rules 232 to 234 of Civil Rules of Practice to issue a cheque in favour of the petitioner/G.Satyanarayana Reddy S/o (late) Koti Reddy for amount of Rs.6,86,025/- towards the satisfaction of the decree debt (compensation).
The facts leading to filing of this petition are briefly as follows:

In LAOP No.45 of 2015 filed by the Land Acquisition Officer and Revenue Divisional Office, Vijayawada against Smt.G.Venkamma w/o (late) Koti Reddy, and her elder son G.Satyanarayana Reddy filed a petition in I.A.No.932 of 2016 under Order XXII Rule 4 CPC.
Since the petition was dismissed, he filed CRP.No.4946 of 2018 before this High Court.
The same was allowed on 31.08.2018, as the LAO as well as the contesting respondents reported no objection, yet the tribunal dismissed the petition.
Guntaka Satyanarayana Reddy, vs Land Acquisition Officer And Revenue ...

sentences.text:
on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97989450/
1

The objection for impleading was taken on the ground that the registered will dated 07.10.2015 executed by G.Venkamma refers to bequest for A,B,C scheduled properties, whereas the matter relating to compensation amount was mentioned in page No.3 of the Will but without bequest of the same in favour of G.Satyanarayana Reddy and since the Will does not cover the land acquired, G.Satyanarayana Reddy cannot claim the whole amount of compensation, if the property is not covered, the petitioner's mother could not have permitted to withdraw the compensation and that what applies to the petitioner's mother will equally applies to the petitioner and therefore, the revision petition was allowed.

According to the petitioner, the 1st respondent in the main LAOP filed a memo on 05.10.2015 requesting the Court to release the compensation amount in favour of the 2nd claimant as she had no objection and accordingly the Court closed the LAOP proceedings on 28.10.2015.

G.Satyanarayana Reddy further filed I.A.No.1274 of 2015 to add him as legal representative on 25.11.2015 and the petition was closed with a direction to file a cheque petition as per the order dated 12.01.2016.
Accordingly, he filed a petition in G.L.No.856 of 2016 dated 12.12.2016 for issuance of cheque.
He further stated that I.A.No.2073 of 2018 is filed to send for the amounts by cancelling the fixed deposit receipt and the same was allowed on 15.11.2018.
Subsequently, third parties filed petition under Order I Rule 10 CPC, which was disposed on 25.08.2018.
Thus, he filed the present petition in I.A.No.1369 of 2022 for issuance of cheque for Rs.6,86,025/-.

While so,
I.A.No.1370 of 2022 was filed by his brother G.Anji Reddy, as a third party to issue cheque for Rs.3,43,012/-, in which G.Satyanarayana Reddy is the 3rd respondent.
A common order was passed on 07.03.2023 in I.A.Nos.1369 and 1370 of 2022.

The following points were considered:
1.
Whether the petitioner in I.A.No.1369 of 2022 is entitled for issuance of Rs.6,86,025/-?

2. Whether the petitioner in I.A.No.1370 of 2022 is entitled for issuance of Rs.3,43,012/-?
3. To what relief?
3.

The case of G.Anji Reddy is that his mother G.Venkamma was permitted by the Court vide its order dated 28.10.2015 to withdraw Rs.5,94,759/-, however she died on 31.10.2015 and intestate having executed a registered will dated 10.07.2015 giving right to his brother G.Satyanarayana Reddy to continue with the land acquisition proceedings and take steps for enhancement of compensation amount and the Will was acted upon.

He further stated that the properties shown as A,B,C schedules in the Will did not contain the property acquired by the land acquisition officer and that since the compensation amount was already fixed by the Court, there is no need for G.Satyanarayana Reddy to continue with the proceedings as mentioned in the Will.

It is further contended that since there is no bequest in the Will with regard to the compensation amount, it shall be deemed that she died intestate in respect of said amount and consequently the amount of compensation devolves on her legal heirs.

sentences.text: 2 Thus, he makes a claim for half of such amount and filed the cheque petition for release of Rs.3,43,012/- in his favour.

4. On the other hand, the contention of G.Satyanarayana Reddy is that he is entitled to the whole amount of compensation payable to his mother by virtue of the Will in his favour and that he was added as a legal representative by virtue of the order in CRP.No.4296 of 2018 and consequently on 10.10.2018 a memo was filed and later he was added as a legal representative and therefore his brother G.Anji Reddy cannot make claim over the compensation amount lying in the Court account as a share holder without specific orders from a competent Court.

It is further contended that even if G.Satyanarayana Reddy receives any compensation claim of the amount G.Anji Reddy will have right to claim from G.Satyanarayana Reddy.
5.
While passing the common order, the Court decided point no.1 as both points 1 and 2 have commonality.
The result in I.A.Nos.1369 and 1370 of 2022 are shown under the heading "point no.2".
It appears that the order containing the reasons for point nos.1 and 2 were intended to be decided together and thus, the result must be under "point no.3".
6. Now, G.Satyanarayana Reddy alone filed this revision petition against the order in I.A.No.1369 of 2022.
He did not choose to challenge the order in I.A.No.1370 OF 2022, though, he is 3 rd respondent thereto.
The learned counsel for the petitioner/G.Satyanarayana Reddy submits that no revision was preferred against the order in I.A.No.1370 of 2022 by the petitioner therein i.e., G.Anji Reddy.
He further submitted that no civil proceeding has been instituted so far by either G.Satyanarayana Reddy or G.Anji Reddy.

7. In the impugned order, it was held that the facts that G.Venkamma executed a registered will on 10.07.2015 and that she died on 31.10.2015 and further that the Will was acted upon are admitted and that the only dispute between the petitioners in both the petitions is that G.Satyanarayana Reddy, being the elder son, is claiming the entire compensation amount in terms of the Will,
whereas G.Anji Reddy is claiming half of the said amount.

The Court observed that since there are rival claims between both the petitioners with regard to entitlement of the compensation amount in view of contention of G.Anji Reddy that the mother died intestate in so far as the amount of compensation is concerned, because there is no express bequest of such amount in favour of G.Satyanarayana Reddy or anyone, both the parties were directed to resolve their dispute before a competent civil Court.
Thus, the Court held that both the petitioners are not entitled to issuance of cheque and resultantly both the petitions were dismissed.
8. As already noted, it is only G.Satyanarayana Reddy who filed the present revision petition.
As can be seen from the undisputed facts G.Satyanarayana Reddy and G.Anji Reddy are claiming as legal representatives of G.Venkamma.
While G.Satyanarayana Reddy is claiming the whole amount of compensation by virtue of the Will, his brother G.Anji Reddy is asking for half of the amount of compensation towards his share.
Thus, the right of G.Satyanarayana Reddy in the compensation amount, to the extent of half of the amount being legal heir, is not under contest by his brother G.Anji Reddy.
Therefore, instead of dismissing the cheque petition for the whole amount, he can be permitted to withdraw half of the amount of compensation which he is undisputedly entitled.

3 9.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that by virtue of the Will and since G.Satyanarayana Reddy is a respondent in main LAOP, he can be permitted to receive the other half of the amount of compensation also subject to right of his brother G.Anji Reddy which he has to work out in a separate civil suit.

10. This proposition cannot be accepted for the reasons that the finding in I.A.No.1370 of 2022 directing the parties to resolve their dispute through civil Court has not been challenged by G.Satyanarayana Reddy, though he is party to that petition and the order therein is binding on him.
Of course, such a finding is common in both petitions in I.A.Nos.1369 and 1370 of 2022.

The challenge made against order in I.A.No.1369 of 2022 before this Court is not enough to challenge the very same finding in I.A.No.1370 of 2022, since the unchallenged finding therein remains in conflict with the other.

As such, this Court is not inclined to consider the question whether the petitioner/G.Satyanarayana Reddy can be permitted to take the entire amount of compensation subject to the right of his brother G.Anji Reddy to be worked out in civil proceedings.

However,
since the petitioner is entitled to half of the amount of compensation by virtue of his heirship irrespective of the Will, it is open for him to receive the said amount.
11. In the result, the revision petition is allowed partly.

The order impugned in the revision petition in I.A.No.1369 of 2022 is set aside partly and the order dismissing the petition therein is set aside and the trial Court is directed to issue cheque to the petitioner G.Satyanarayana Reddy S/o late Koti Reddy for an amount of Rs.3,43,012.50/- together with proportionate interest, if any accrued thereon till the date of issue of cheque.
The other legal formalities of the issuance for cheque shall be completed by the petitioner as per the direction of the trial Court.
Miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand vacated.
Interlocutory applications, if any, shall stand closed.
